<store>
Name: Fernhill Coffee Supply
Sells: Fernhill Coffee Supply sells home coffee brewing equipment and coffee beans. The range covers pour-over gear (ceramic and stainless steel drippers, size 02 paper filters, stovetop and electric gooseneck kettles, and a brew scale with timer), immersion brewers such as a French press and a cold brew jar, and manual and electric burr grinders. It also sells single-origin coffee beans from Fernhill Roastery in 250 g and 1 kg bags, whole bean or ground.
Audience: People who brew coffee at home, especially by pour-over or immersion, and who want to grind, weigh and control water temperature themselves. Some products, such as the single-dose flat-burr grinder and the temperature-hold kettle, suit buyers who care about precise brewing.
Tone: expert
Never say: —
</store>

<topic>

<products>
  P1: Hand Grinder, conical steel burrs (Grinder)

    F2: The Fernhill Hand Grinder is a manual grinder.
    F3: The Fernhill Hand Grinder has 38 mm hardened stainless steel conical burrs.
    F4: The Fernhill Hand Grinder has external click adjustment with 30 settings.
    F5: The Fernhill Hand Grinder's settings range from espresso to French press.

    F27: The French Press makes about 4 mugs.
    F28: The French Press has a four-layer mesh filter.

    F33: The Cold Brew Jar is made by Fernhill.
    F34: The Cold Brew Jar is a glass jar.
    F35: The Cold Brew Jar has a fine stainless steel filter basket.

    F37: The Cold Brew Jar makes 1.5 litres of concentrate.
    F38: The Cold Brew Jar has an airtight lid.
    F39: The Cold Brew Jar fits in a fridge door.

content.text: {"title":"Coffee Grind Size Chart: The Right Grind for Pour-Over, French Press and Cold Brew","angle":"The reader will know which grind size suits each home brewing method, how to recognise it by eye and taste, and how to dial it in on a burr grinder.","sections":[{"heading":"The coffee grind size chart at a glance","covers":"A chart from extra fine (Turkish) through fine (espresso), medium-fine (cone pour-over), medium (flat-bottom drippers), coarse (French press) to extra coarse (cold brew), with texture comparisons like flour, table salt, sea salt and cracked pepper, and why contact time drives the choice.","facts":[]},{"heading":"Why a burr grinder makes the chart work","covers":"Uniform particles versus blade grinders, why consistency matters more than any single setting, and how click and stepless adjustment let you repeat and fine-tune a grind.","facts":["F1","F3","F4","F5","F41","F42","F44"]},{"heading":"Pour-over: medium-fine for cones, medium for flat beds","covers":"Cone drippers with one large outlet rely on grind to control flow, so go medium-fine. Flat-bottom drippers with small holes run slower and suit a slightly coarser medium grind. Includes a starting dose and a drawdown time to aim for.","facts":["F18","F19","F16","F53","F54","F55","F9"]},{"heading":"French press: coarse and even","covers":"Why a coarse, even grind suits a four-minute immersion, how fines cause sludge and bitterness, and how the mesh filter handles a coarse grind.","facts":["F23","F28","F22","F27"]},{"heading":"Cold brew: extra coarse for a long steep","covers":"Why a 12 to 18 hour cold steep needs the coarsest setting, typical coffee-to-water ratios for concentrate, and how to dilute it.","facts":["F36","F37","F40","F35"]},{"heading":"Dialling in: reading your cup","covers":"How to adjust from the chart: sour and thin means grind finer, bitter and harsh means grind coarser. Change one setting at a time, and grind fresh for each brew.","facts":["F6","F43","F46"]}],"products":["P1","P2","P3","P4"],"links":["P1","P5","P2","P6","P3","P4","L1","L2","L3","L4"]}
